title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Laura Chen
content:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood’s core people policies and practical guides for engineers and cross-functional teams: a concise description of 'working at Redwood', role families and career ladders, primary benefits and perks, our hiring and new-hire onboarding flow, and a quick reference for the internal tools you will use daily. It is intended as the canonical place for questions about joining, growing at, and operating inside Redwood.

1) Working at Redwood — values and expectations

Intro: Redwood is an engineering-first, product-driven company. Our culture centers on ownership, trust, and clear communication. We expect everyone to deliver high-quality work, prioritize customer-facing reliability, and make decisions that scale.

Core behaviors we value:
- Ship with care: prioritize reliable rollouts, measurable impact, and clear documentation.
- Be data-informed: validate design and product choices with metrics, benchmarks, and small experiments.
- Help others: mentor peers, contribute to runbooks, and review PRs promptly.
- Communicate proactively: status updates, postmortems, and design notes should be clear and timely.

Working norms:
- Core hours: flexible, with a recommended overlap window 10:00–15:00 PT for synchronous collaboration.
- Meetings: keep meetings outcome-oriented and invite only those who need to make or be informed of decisions.
- Feedback: use regular 1:1s and quarterly reviews; continuous feedback is encouraged through Slack and peer review.

2) Roles and career ladders (summary)

Role families at Redwood:
- Engineering (Serving runtime, Infra, Platform, Developer Experience, SRE)
- Product (PM, Design, Product Ops)
- Applied ML & Research
- Customer Success & Support
- Go-to-market (Sales, Marketing)
- People Ops, Finance & Legal, Security

Career ladder structure (common elements across ladders):
- IC levels: IC1 (New grad/early), IC2 (contributor), IC3 (senior), IC4 (staff), IC5 (principal/architect)
- Manager levels: Mgr1 (first-time manager), Mgr2 (experienced manager), Dir (director)

What each level implies (short):
- IC2: Delivers features with mentorship; owns small services/components and writes clear design docs.
- IC3: End-to-end ownership of product areas, mentors others, contributes to architecture.
- IC4+: Shapes cross-team architecture, leads major initiatives, measurable company-level impact.

Promotion rubric (summary):
1. Scope: increased ownership across larger areas or teams.
2. Impact: measurable product/operational outcomes.
3. Craft: technical or role-specific excellence (code quality, design, GTM execution).
4. Leadership: influence without authority, mentorship, and cross-team collaboration.

Resources:
- For engineering-specific ladders and competencies see: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/sdk-guides and /confluence/eng-platform/roadmap (linked pages).
- Promotion packet checklist: updated CV, two peer feedbacks, manager recommendation, and a documented impact report.

3) Benefits and perks (high level)

Standard benefits (US & selected regions):
- Health: medical, dental, and vision plans with Redwood covering a portion of premiums.
- Time off: 20 days PTO (prorated), companywide holidays (10 days), and 6 weeks parental leave for primary caregivers.
- Financial: 401(k) matching (US), equity grants with regular refresh cycles, and competitive salary bands.
- Wellness: monthly wellness stipend, EAP (employee assistance program), and monthly mental health sessions.

Perks and remote-friendly support:
- Home office stipend for new hires and refresh every 2 years.
- Flexible equipment policy: choose preferred laptop (M-series Mac or equivalent Windows) and peripherals.
- Learning budget: $1,500/year per employee; team budgets for conferences on approval.
- Commuter benefits and coworking credits in major hubs.

Benefits table (summary):
| Category | What Redwood provides | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Medical | Multiple plans; employer contribution | Varies by country and level |
| PTO | 20 days + holidays | Manager discretion for roll-over up to 5 days |
| Parental leave | 6 weeks primary, 4 weeks secondary | Supplemental options available |
| Equity | Annual refresh + new-hire grant | Standard vesting 4y w/ 1y cliff |

How to use and request benefits:
- Submit benefit elections in BambooHR within 30 days of start date.
- For parental leave, notify People Ops 90 days in advance where possible; returns include a formal RTW (return to work) plan.

4) Hiring and onboarding (overview)

Hiring principles:
- Candidate experience: clear expectations, timely feedback, and transparent compensation.
- Role-fit focus: evaluate for current role and growth potential; use structured rubrics.
- Interview loop: hiring manager screen, technical assessment (take-home or live), cross-functional interviews (product/peer), and final leadership conversation for senior candidates.

Standard interview loop (engineering example):
1. Recruiter screen (culture and logistics)
2. Hiring manager technical screen (30–45 min)
3. Take-home or coding exercise (48–72 hours turnaround)
4. Onsite / loop (4–5 interviews): technical, system design, cross-functional, and bar-raiser
5. Debrief and recommendation -> compensation approval -> offer

Onboarding flow (first 90 days):
- Day 0–1: Offer acceptance flows through HR systems; equipment order and account provisioning.
- Week 1: Welcome orientation, People Ops intro, security & compliance training, manager 1:1, team kickoff.
- Month 1: Shadowing, first small deliverable, create a 30-60-90 plan with manager.
- Month 2: Begin owning small features, attend product/architecture reviews.
- Month 3: Present a first project or postmortem, feedback checkpoint, and set promotion development goals if applicable.

New-hire checklist (condensed):
- Complete security and compliance trainings within 5 business days.
- Set up MFA and VPN access.
- Join team Slack channels and calendar invites.
- Confirm mentoring buddy assigned.

5) Internal tools quick reference

This section lists primary internal systems and what they are used for. Each tool page contains longer runbooks; links included below.

- Slack: primary team communication. Channels are prefixed by team (e.g., #eng-serving-runtime). Use thread replies and reactions for lightweight coordination.
- Confluence: formal documentation and runbooks (this space). Save design docs and postmortems here.
- GitHub: code hosting and PR workflows. Branch protection enforced on main branches; PR checklist required.
- Jenkins / CI provider: CI runs for builds and integration tests. See eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build for pipeline ownership.
- Datadog / Observability: dashboards and alerts for services. Dashboards are organized by team tags and critical SLOs.
- BambooHR: HR system for benefits elections, time-off requests, and personal info.
- 1Password: company secrets vault; vaults are permissioned by role.
- JIRA: work tracking for larger initiatives. Small tasks can remain in GitHub Issues per team preference.

Common operational commands and snippets (examples):
- Request access to a repo: open a PR to infra-team/access-requests with repo and permission level.
- Create a new Confluence page: use template 'Team RFC' under Confluence > Templates.
- Submit an equipment request: visit IT self-service portal and reference the 'home office' policy.

6) Day-to-day operational guidelines and runbooks

Incident readiness:
- Pager expectations: SRE owns escalation; engineers with on-call responsibilities must follow the oncall playbook in /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks.
- Postmortems: include timeline, root cause, impact, remediation, and owner for follow-ups. All postmortems should be linked from the incident ticket.

Cost and quota awareness:
- Track your service cost by token usage; Redwood Console exposes per-route metrics and cost breakdowns. Include cost expectations in design docs for large model usage.

7) Questions, feedback, and how to propose changes

If you notice missing or out-of-date information:
1. Open a Confluence edit and propose changes inline for minor updates.
2. For significant policy changes, file a PR to the People Ops handbook and add reviewers: @PeopleOps, @Legal (if required).
3. For process or tooling changes, open a RFC in Confluence using the 'Process Change' template and assign owners.
